findings.issue: Team members whose species 404s are silently dropped, so the '<n> of 6' count can disagree with the cookie and a stale name can never be removed via the UI
findings.suggestion: Count from the parsed cookie and either render the failed member as a placeholder with a Remove button, or prune it from the cookie

findings.issue: A non-OK API response rejects through render with no app-level error boundary, so a flaky API shows Next's default error page
findings.suggestion: Add a root error.tsx (and optionally loading.tsx for the heavier pages) so failures degrade gracefully

findings.issue: Default-variety resolution (species.varieties.find(is_default) → getPokemon(idFromUrl)) is duplicated from app/src/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:48-56
findings.suggestion: Extract a getDefaultPokemon(species) helper into lib/api.ts and use it from both pages

findings.issue: Client components type-import from lib/api.ts, a server-only module; it compiles because type imports are erased, but client code now depends on a module it can never value-import
findings.suggestion: Move shared types (CardData, TypeInfo) to a neutral types module so the server/client boundary is explicit in imports

findings.issue: Two different patterns for following server-driven prop changes: useEffect sync here vs render-time state adjustment in game-select.tsx:15-18 and team-toggle.tsx:20-23
findings.suggestion: Standardize on the React-documented render-time adjustment pattern across all three components

findings.issue: Hand-rolled TTL/LRU fetch cache reimplements what Next's data cache with `next: { revalidate: 60 }` provides (justified by the spec's no-build-time-data rule, and well-bounded, but a reviewer will ask)
findings.suggestion: Keep it, but note in the comment why the framework's fetch cache was avoided (no-store + connection() + in-memory TTL), or migrate to `next: { revalidate: 60 }` under the already-forced dynamic rendering

summary: A genuinely well-crafted Next.js 16 App Router app: correct async request APIs, a guarded data layer with a bounded cache and concurrency limiter, and a feature change that fits the existing conventions without a seam. Idiom is current-release accurate, including the deliberate choice of `connection()` + `no-store` over ISR to satisfy the spec's request-time-data requirement. I'd merge as-is; the findings are nits suitable for follow-up.
